newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks seen seen pushing higher.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks seen seen pushing higher.

text.p: Argentine stocks were expected to open firm Tuesday and continue their upward course, dicounting a 25-basis points rise in U.S. interest rates by the Federal Open Market Committee later in the day, dealers said.

"The market priced in a rate increase and began its recovery last week -- now it's gearing up to tackle resistance levels and rally again in April," said analyst Maximiliano Goff at the research department of Banco Rio.
The blue-chip MerVal index rose 1.6 percent Monday to 741.91, extending last week's 2.6 percent rebound.

"The bolsa's recovery is fuelled this week by a much-awaited rebound on Wall Street," Goff said. "It seems the worst is over and Greenspan may have achieved what he wanted even without a rate hike: a more gradual, mild-mannered rise in the New York markets."
Traders said the bolsa continued to be underpinned by a possible debt upgrade by Standard & Poor's in early April.
"What we need now is for (floor) volume to be restored to a daily average of about $30 million -- although that's unlikely to happen until after Easter," another trader said.
The local markets close Thursday and Friday.
